target.name: Lyten
target.founder: Dan Cook, Bharat Sastri, Mike Stuart

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.3B total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Lyten is a Series C materials-science company founded by Dan Cook, Bharat Sastri, and Mike Stuart that has raised $1.33B to date. The private comparable set is limited to a single identified peer, Noveon Magnetics, reflecting the early-stage maturity and specialized nature of frontier materials development. No directly comparable public companies were identified in this sector cohort.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $1.3B capital raised proxy. This approach yields an implied valuation of $2.3B. The 1.7x multiplier reflects median observed progression from Series C financing rounds to subsequent financing events in materials-tech companies, though the limited public comps universe constrains precision.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B (low) to $2.6B (high), with a median point of $2.3B. This range brackets realistic outcomes given Lyten's stage and capital intensity, but carries material uncertainty stemming from the sparse comparable set and the inherent difficulty in benchmarking pre-revenue frontier-materials businesses. Key variables affecting the final valuation include customer adoption trajectories, manufacturing scale-up success, and competitive positioning relative to alternative materials platforms. A broader peer set and forward-looking revenue or unit-economics data would materially improve confidence in this range.
